utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Could you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. This is Case Number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Nicholas Koumjian with Ruth Karper for the Prosecution. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Branko Lukic and Mr. John Ostojic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On purpose, I asked not to bring in the witness because we have to clarify something and not in the presence of the witness. Yesterday, Mr. Koumjian, you -- Yesterday, Mr. Koumjian, you mentioned as regards our present witness that there is a proofing binder that they, meaning the Defence, got with this witness. Could you please explain about the proofing binder and why it is not in the hands of the Judges.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, I corrected myself, I believe later. The proofing binder is an OTP internal document the Defence doesn't have. The Defence has all statements of the witness and all prior testimony of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And what about -- we discussed it before -- the proofing notes, because once again, one can identify a discrepancy between the former statement and what the witness actually said. And I'm not aware that we have any proofing notes on this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, no proofing notes were prepared for this witness. And to be honest, I'm not sure of the discrepancy Your Honour is referring to. I proofed the witness, and although I mentioned a couple things that were outside the testimony to the Defence, I didn't see any discrepancies or significant new material. Undoubtedly he said some things that are not in the prior statement, but no significant new material in the proofing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then, in addition also, in the absence of the witness, yesterday, we admitted into evidence S51. First of all, it was focussed on the map before us. Then we got some informations on the pictures, 11 and 10. But I don't believe it's fair to introduce something into evidence just in the form of "by the way, there are additional pictures," and they are, as it's on one piece of paper, admitted into evidence as one entire document, knowing very well that in part, we have already these documents in the list of -- in the file of Prijedor photographs before us. And I think, for example, when discussing the way of destruction and the degree of destruction of the mosque in Kozarac, one shouldn't refer to this small picture we have here on 11, but we have other pictures of the mosque available. And we have numerous pictures of the camps available. In the past, the Office of the Prosecutor always asked a person detained in a camp where did he live, where was the situation, actual situation of an incident that happened. But it wasn't the case today. And this would bring us to the situation that at the end of the day, we have to once again repeat, in part, the interrogation of a witness ex officio by the Trial Chamber. And I think this is not in the spirit of this adversarial procedure. And my point is why didn't the Prosecutor introduce the other remarkable photographs, for example, of the mosque, of the Trnopolje camp, through the witness before us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, part of the reason is trying to finish with the witness in a reasonable period of time. We can go through with each witness in Omarska, the various rooms they were held in, have each witness describe the camp location. My understanding from some of the Court's -- Trial Chamber's previous remarks is the Court did not want to repeat testimony that was unchallenged. Any time I show a document to a witness, obviously that takes some period of time. Regarding the photographs, the next witness the Prosecution has scheduled is an investigator who would testify to the source of the photographs, when they were taken, who took the photographs. We could show all the pictures, most of our witnesses are familiar with many of the pictures that we have. But it would greatly lengthen the proceedings. We are really trying to focus on the issues that are most in dispute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Respectfully, my objections, for example, picture 8 we discussed yesterday. We have a very small picture, and of course the question was raised by the Defence: When was this picture taken? And we did discuss this situation, of course, in Omarska at length, but never until now the situation of the buildings in Trnopolje. And we have the same picture in this folder, but in a better way and in a way easier to understand and easier to be explained. And I don't think it's a good idea to let things be explained by an investigator, when we have a person here having lived in the concrete circumstances of this environment. Because from the point of view, let's say, of a Defence counsel, I would contest pictures of the interior of a camp. It should be explained by a witness. Was it really the situation the witness saw and experienced at that time he was there under detention, and it's not relevant at all what an investigator saw in 1996 or 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sorry, is Your Honour waiting for a response?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I understand that's Your Honour's point of view. I conducted the examination focussing on what I thought was most at issue. But we can show these witnesses the photographs, each of them each of the camps they were in. I would be happy to do it with this witness and with the witnesses to come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it also be in the interest of the Defence, for example, the degree of destruction of a mosque, the interior of a camp, if it's really reliable information. We all know that today, pictures can lie, and therefore I personally don't want to have introduced this kind of evidence. Let's call it evidence by an investigator. And as far as I know, until now, we went through the details of Omarska, but not Trnopolje, not Manjaca. And therefore, the possibility should not be omitted. Of course, you can leave it for the Judges if you so want.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: We didn't go through the physical layouts and the photographs of the Trnopolje camp, but this witness discussed the conditions that he was detained under only for a couple of days. And the issue that we feel is very, very important, and I believe in dispute regarding Trnopolje, and that's that it was in fact a detention camp and people were not free to leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So do you want to continue with the examination --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I was going to ask anyway, because I also noticed -- I realised after the examination that I forgot one very fundamental question regarding the witness's background, and that is his ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. I think it would be appropriate, and it would assist the work of the Bench, we discussed it before this hearing, if you can also put the questions to the witness underlying the pictures we have available in the file on Prijedor photographs. Any observations by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I be excused for 10, 15 minutes, please, to bring some materials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: No doubt. You need a break?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No, no. I'll leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If the Court has asked for an observation, I do have one if the Court permits, and that is particularly with -- since we're discussing the issue of the Trnopolje camp and namely picture 8 on Exhibit S51. If the Prosecutor, to the extent they do have a picture aerial or otherwise reflecting the southern portion of the camp, we do have the enlargement showing only from this border. But we think, and we will try to obtain that as well, but for the purposes of the trial and the proceedings here, that if the aerial view was taken and entire the complex, both the south, north, east, west can be seen, then that might enhance the appreciation of the area for both sides. So, to the extent that they have that. I haven't seen it yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Indeed. And also the OTP may understand, it can't be a guessing game for the Judges. To see here pictures 5-8 to 5-H, and yes, as the Defence correctly stated, to guess what is what, we have additional -- it's said that this should be additional pictures from the Trnopolje camp. And therefore, we need some explanation. And this should go through a witness having experienced the situation there. And the additional information you wanted as to the dates when the pictures were taken, you can identify them on these pictures. And evidently, once again, one has to say that there is a significant change of the mosque on the one picture, 11, and the other picture we have before us, taken in 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We just weren't sure, Your Honour, at the top of --, when we examined this initially, whether they were exactly the same or not. So that's why we just inquired on those dates on this picture. We will go back and make that study and do the comparison. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So is the Defence prepared? May we continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We may, but I have one other preliminary comment. And I'd like a little guidance from the Court if you would be so kind. And it involves S51P which was marked as confidential. So I'm not sure if I can discuss any portion of it now and would ask, perhaps, we go into private session for that, because I do have some questions not just from the witness but I'd like some guidance from the Court on this as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let's turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: (redacted).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness P.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Witness P, I neglected to ask you yesterday, would you tell the Tribunal what your ethnicity is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm a Bosniak, and my religion is Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Witness P, I would now to show you a series of photographs, the first --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm going to show the witness. I don't know if the registry has them. The photographs labelled 2, 5, and 9. These series on the index of Prijedor photographs in Exhibit 15. The ERN on the 2A is 00393467. On 2B, it's 00393191. 2C, 00393202. 2D, 00393081. 2E, 00394827. And 2F, 00393193. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Witness P, before you is on Exhibit S15, photograph 2A which is -- can you please tell us if you recognise the structures depicted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recognise the old cinema. It's depicted here on this photograph. This building here is the elementary school in Kozarac. I can't be specific about this mosque here because I cannot say where this photograph was taken from. But I'm sure it's one of the mosques in Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, for the record, can the record reflect referred first to the structure in -- the photograph in the top right, then the bottom right, and finally the mosque was the left-hand side of the exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to now show you photograph 2B of this exhibit. Do you recognise the structure depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this is the same mosque that we saw on the previous photograph, only now it has been destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And you're not sure which mosque this is. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it is the Dera mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to show you photograph 2C. Do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the remnants of some of -- of one of the many mosques in Kozarac, but I can't really say which one it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now I'd like to show you 2D. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps, on the basis of this old tree here, it could be the mosque in Kamicani, but I'm not sure. It's a linden tree.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to show you 2D. And for the record, the witness's last answer was referring to 2C. Showing you now 2D, do you recognise what's depicted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this picture, you can see the church on the old Prijedor/Banja Luka Road. It's in fact the only church in Kozarac. It's a Serbian church.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you see that church prior to the conflict and after the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had seen the church before the conflict and after. Its state remained the same, but a new church is being built next to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'd now like to show you 2E. Witness P, do you recognise what's depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Kozarac area. The photograph was taken from the side -- I don't know the exact position where the photograph was taken, but on the basis of the school and the mosque and the new school, I'm absolutely sure that it is Kozarac, Kozarac area.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You indicated the mosque. Can you point again to the mosque that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case, this is the mosque that I think is the one that we saw on the pictures a little while ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Witness P, are you familiar with a mosque known as Mutnicka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both Mutnik and Dera mosques were within 50 metres -- 500 metres of each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you see the Mutnik mosque after the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you see it when you returned to Kozarac in 1997?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was no longer there at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Have you heard, Witness P, of the Kalata mosque?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you see that mosque after the attack on Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did you see that mosque in 1997 when you returned?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was generally known that no mosque in the territory of Kozarac, the total of 16 or 17 mosques, remained in their normal state.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I'd now like to show you a series of photographs from the same exhibit, photographs A through H. And for the record, 5A will read sequentially the ERN numbers 02147089, B is 00389747, C is 02147092, D is 0214 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please slow down with the numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Showing you first 5A. Witness P, do you recognise the area depicted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the picture of Trnopolje, the school. This here is the old hall with the auxiliary buildings, and this here was the shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Where were the persons detained kept, or where did they sleep in the Trnopolje camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: The entire school was full, this hall here, behind this area. And all over this area, there were tents, vehicles, trailers, cars. It was all full of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And for the record, the second building -- the witness first referred to the school in the bottom right, and then referred to the white building in the bottom left of the photograph. I'm showing you now 5B. Witness, do you recognise and can you tell us what is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's the same school in Trnopolje that I was just talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm showing you now 5C. Can you explain, if you recognise this, what it is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a building in Trnopolje. Behind this building is the hall that I was talking about. The camp commander, the Trnopolje camp commander, the Red Cross, and the so-called infirmary were located in the front part of the building. The infirmary was operating at that time in the Trnopolje camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Showing you now 5D. Can you tell us what is depicted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a small shop. It is here in the extension of the building that we just saw on the previous photograph. It is the extension to the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: What was this building used for when you were at the camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my stay, the shop was open for the two or three days. And after I left, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Showing -- when you say it was open, what do you mean? Were detainees inside that shop, or what was it used for? Were goods sold?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: One could still buy the remaining items that were in the shop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now showing you 5E. Can you tell us if you recognise what is depicted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this photograph was taken in front of this centre in Trnopolje, and across the road -- I don't know whether there were a cafe here or a shop. I'm not sure. But at any rate, it is a picture depicting Trnopolje.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Does the usher have the photographs labelled 7? I know I didn't ask for them earlier. Let's go to 9 for now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Going to photograph 9A, I'm going to skip the rest of the 5 photographs. I'm sorry, I will go back to those three photographs just to see something. I'm going to show you three photographs. The usher is now going to put on 5F. Just tell me if you know the person depicted. 5F, ending in 2537 is the ERN. Do you know this man?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't think you'll recognise someone's back, so going then to 5H. Do you recognise this person depicted in the photograph the usher is now showing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now going to photograph 9, series 9. And I will read slowly the ERN numbers of these six photographs. They are 9A, 01002444, 9B, 02123687, 9D, apparently there's no C, 00409597, 9E, 00409596, 9F, 00409592, and 9G, 00409598. Showing you first photograph 9A, Witness P, can you tell us what is depicted.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you point out on that photograph some of the structures where people were detained?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most of the people were held during the night on the first floor of this building here. Some of the people were held in a small garage behind the kitchen. And a part were held in the central part of the kitchen which was called the glass house. And some of the women were held during the day in one of the corners of the kitchen. A certain number of people were held here on the pista, during the day. And in the early days of the existence of the camp, some slept in the kitchen. And during the second half of the existence of the camp, they slept here in this building on the floor, this building was called the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: For the record, the witness first referred to the large L-shaped, somewhat reddish in colour building in the centre of the photograph. He then referred to the more orange-coloured smaller structures to the left of the photograph. He referred to the pista as being the area between those structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Witness P, where was the hangar again that you referred to? Can you point to that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two floors here, two storeys. On the upper floor, people were housed throughout the building, and some were held on the ground floor in the hangar. You could also see the white house, the red house, and here there should be a transformer station. I think it's the little white building here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just for the record, the witness pointed to the white house as a white structure in the centre of the photograph; the red house as a building just to the right of the large centre structure reddish in colour, and just below and to the right of the large reddish structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And Witness, I'm still having a little trouble with the hangar. Can you point again where the hangar is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: We called the structure the hangar. It was for the people who stayed on the pista. And they also then stayed in an open structure here to the left as you got in. It was an open structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Showing you now 9B. Do you recognise what's depicted?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen these beds in my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Going now to 9D. I believe I have a different one. It should end in 9597.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can the usher tell us the ERN of that. For the record, this is 9E.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise what's depicted on 9E, this photograph that's now to your right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a scale model of the Omarska camp. The white house, the red house, the garage with the hangar, and the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So to be clear again, the garage with the hangar is the building on the right-hand side of the photograph. Is that correct? Can you point to it again, to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: We called these rooms here on the ground floor the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The witness pointed to the large structure to the left of the photograph with the open white spaces.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And can you show where the white house and red house are on these photographs.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: The white house. The red house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Indicating the small white house to the centre of the -- top centre of the photograph, and the very top left of the photograph, the red house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, showing you -- why don't we put the next one up, and I'll read out the letter after I see the photograph. This is ERN number 9592. This is photograph 9F of S15. And Witness, do you recognise this as just a different view of the same structures?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can you tell us, where were you kept during your stay at Omarska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here, in this corner. The room on the top floor, the windows here, that's where we were for a while. And during the later stage of my stay in the camp, I slept somewhere here in the offices, that we opened by force in order to have more room to sleep in.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The night that you saw the people from Hambarine being shot, can you tell us which room were you in that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in one of the rooms here on the top floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Indicating on the large structure on the photograph, to the left of the structure, on the portion of the building facing the camera.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And can you point out, if it's -- if the area is depicted on this photograph, where the bodies were that you saw lying on the ground.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: The bodies were scattered in groups in the area around the white house. Behind it. Over a large area because the number of bodies was quite large.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, I'd like that photograph 9G, which 9598.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Witness, do you recognise this photograph as being a model of the Omarska building with the roof or ceiling removed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't really understand the layout. I don't really see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Did we ever find 9597? D.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Witness, again, do you recognise this as the Omarska building?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Excuse me, that's not 9597.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Witness, can you tell us if you recognise what is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the kitchen in the Omarska camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Where exactly is the kitchen? Can you point to it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the kitchen. That's where we ate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Indicating the glass area to the left of the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Was there a guard post somewhere in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: The guard post was located on the roof of the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd now like to show you some photographs of the -- labelled 7A, 7B, and 7C. Witness, showing you 7A which has the ERN 00396712. Do you Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the Manjaca camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: What part of the camp is that? From where the person is taking the picture, is he standing inside or outside of the camp? Can you tell?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is a mirror image, it seems to me. Well, on the basis of this plaque here, the person who took the photograph stood in front of the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. And where is this in relation to where the buses, that you were on that transported you to Manjaca, stopped?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: This location -- well, we may have been about 50 metres away to the right from this place. That's where we were, on a meadow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, showing you 7B, do you recognise what is depicted on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of the boxes in one of the barns where the prisoners were held. There was another row of prisoners here, another there, and there were also prisoners on the higher level, and there was another level which was level with this one that he is depicted here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. I noticed people have their shoes off. Does that have any significance? Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, because of the intense heat in the first few days, and in order to freshen up a little, people would take off their shoes and put them on the concrete or on the gravel to rest a bit, to rest their feet. There was no special rule requiring us to take off our shoes, but most people did take off their shoes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. For the record, this photograph has the ERN number of 00464997.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Now, showing you 7C, 00456983, can you tell us what is depicted in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this picture, you can see the prisoners in one of the barns in the Manjaca camp. It is -- this was taken from an elevated position of the barn, and it covers the central part of the barn.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I would at this time -- well, this is already in -- Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it's necessary that we go immediately and proceed with giving these exhibits the correct numbers. Are there any objections against the admission into evidence of these pictures?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then if the registry could, please, confirm the following: Picture 2A should be S15-4. 2B, S15-5. 2C, S15-6. 2D, S15-7. 2E, S15-8. 5A, S15-9. 5B, S15-10. 5C, S15-11. 5D, S15-12. 5E, S15-13. 5F, S15-14. 5G, S15-15. 5H, S15-16. Now we have a problem, I believe.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I don't think, was 5G presented to the witness? I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: That wasn't shown, the back of the prisoner was not shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So 5G, let us proceed. We had 5F as S15-14. Then we continue with 5H. Correct? S15-15. Right. Then we continue with 9A as S15-16. 9B, S15-17. 9D was already previously admitted as S15-3. Same was true for 9E. That was S15-2. But we have to proceed now with 9F. That is S15-18. 9G, S15-19. And then finally, 7A, S15-20. 7B, S15-21. 7C, S15-22. Can this be confirmed.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. This is confirmed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. I think it's necessary to have a break before we start the cross-examination, and I want explicitly to thank you, Witness P, that you gave us another insight relating that what you told us yesterday to the pictures we saw. We have never been there, unfortunately, but it's for us to get a very real picture of that you have experienced at that time. Thank you for this. The trial stands adjourned until 4.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Mr. President, could I request permission to ask regarding one photograph, that I realised when the Court was doing the marking, I had talked about but had not shown to the witness, and that would be 2F.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I can see no objections, so please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Witness, showing you 2F, which is ERN number 00393193, do you recognise what is depicted on the photograph?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I see destroyed houses, but I don't know in which part of Kozarac they are located.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Is the scene depicted in this photograph typical or atypical of how Kozarac looked after the conflict?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what Kozarac looked like a year or two prior to the takeover of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness, as I understood your answer from the interpretation, you said this is what it looked like, the photograph in front of you, before the takeover?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps you could restate your answer. This is what Kozarac looked like when?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, 1997, this is -- was the state of Kozarac then, so this was the year -- a year after the take -- a few years following the takeover of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You're talking about in 1997 when you returned to Kozarac, this is what you saw typically. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we now finally turn to the cross-examination, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President..

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness P, my name is John Ostojic, and along with Mr. Branko Lukic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Good afternoon, Witness P, my name is John Ostojic, and along with Mr. Branko Lukic, we represent Dr. Milomir Stakic. I'm going to ask you a series of questions here today. If at any time you don't understand my question or would like to elaborate on any of the questions, please, as the president of the Chamber has indicated earlier, please feel free to do so. Is that fair enough?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Preliminarily, sir, I'd like to ask you if you recall giving a- statement to the ICTY on or about August 26th through August 30th, 1994, statement which was signed on or about September 1st, 1994.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the statement -- I gave the statement -- I don't know which year exactly. This may be correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness P. I'm going to show you a statement in a little bit. I just have some preliminary questions in connection with that. Sir, at any time prior or subsequent to the statement that you gave to the ICTY, did you give a statement or were you interviewed by any governmental entity in connection with you being detained in Omarska in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that my first official statement was in the year 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And was the statement that you gave in 1994 a statement that you gave to the governmental agencies of the Republic of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At any time, sir, did you give any such statement to a governmental entity on behalf or represented by the Republic of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, only if the people in 1994 lied to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand your answer, Witness P. Would you help clarify it for me, if you don't mind.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is only possible if the people in 1994 lied about their identity.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. I understand. Thank you. Sir, do you remember a gentleman who was interviewing you during this 1994 statement by the name of Michael Keegan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So is it fair to state, sir, as you sit here, do you remember any of the individuals who interviewed you on or about August of 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was the translator. That was one person. And I'm sure some foreigners were there, so I had no doubts that these were institutions that were not within the frameworks of the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: All I'm seeking, Mr. Witness P, is whether or not you gave any other statements other than the one statement in 1994, if you remember.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'd like, with the Court's permission, to go into private session to have the witness or ask the witness some questions in connection with Exhibit Number S52. And also, if I'm permitted, for the record, during our prior private session, I referenced this exhibit as S51P. I was notified by the Registrar that I incorrectly identified that exhibit, so to the extent possible, if I can just make a note that during that discussion, I was referencing the two-page document, correctly identified as S52.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It was quite clear that it was a fata demonstratio [phoen], but nevertheless, I believe in the interest of the witness, we should go into closed session, because it could be necessary to put this document on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Now it's confirmed. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness P, with respect to the war in 1991 in Croatia, is it true that in your statement that you stated, in fact, that the Muslims had fought on the Croatian side, and the Serbians felt an enmity to the Muslims, as a result of them having fought on the Croatian side -- and that can be found on page 4, first full paragraph of your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if all the Muslims fought on the Croatian side during the war between Croatia and Yugoslavia in 1991, or some, or a few?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have such information. Some individuals did, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, whether there were any mobilisations called by the JNA or the federal former Yugoslavia in 1991?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even though it may have been called, I did not respond to go and fight in Croatia, although the Serbs went to fight in Croatia voluntarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The answer that I received, sir -- and I need to just have a little clarification on it -- was it voluntary or was it a mandatory mobilisation that was called for the residents of the area in which you resided in 1991, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if Alija Izetbegovic in April or May of 1992, whether he announced a call for mobilisation at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never did hear this statement, and over the last few months, we had no contact with him. So I didn't see or hear any such declarations or statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. If I may ask the Court's permission to have the usher present to Witness P Exhibit S51, or S51P, whichever one is available.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If we are in open session, it has to be S51.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: S51. Thank you. Thank you. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Witness P, in connection with this S51, I'd like to ask you some questions, with respect to Kozara which we see in the centre of the picture, as well as the red lines which indicate the main road from Prijedor to Banja Luka. But first, let me ask you about the town in which you lived in. There's something that I saw, I believe, in your statement called a "Mjesna Zajednica". Do you know what that is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an institution where the registry office was housed, I mean the Kozarac registry office and where marriages were performed, various cultural events. There was also the old-age pensioners' home on the other side of that building. So it was a building, a public building.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: (redacted) that also were separate from the Kozarac Mjesna Zajednica such as Gornji or Donja Jakupovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know for certain for some areas. Kozarusa had its own. I'm not sure about whether Babici and Jakupovici had their own. Kevljani had their own smaller branch, which was again subordinate through Omarska or through Kamicani to Prijedor municipality. I'm not sure what the structure was like. They existed in some places; in some other places, there weren't any. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, I'm going to discuss with you now, if I may, the issue of checkpoints in the area that was covered yesterday in some detail. I hope not to repeat any of the questions, and I apologise in advance to the extent that I do. But if you can bear with me, I'd appreciate it very much. Were Muslim checkpoints, Witness P, set up in the area of Kozarac before April 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, there were joint checkpoints manned by the Territorial Defence, the old Territorial Defence which had members both from Serbs, Muslims, and Croats, and which was armed with the old weapons that the Territorial Defence had.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So is it fair to say, then, that in the Kozarac area, was there more than one checkpoint, whether it be manned by the Serbs, the Muslims, or a combination of the two, prior to April 30th, 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Having travelled, as you've indicated in your direct testimony here yesterday, to and from Banja Luka in connection with your business, can you identify for us, on this main road identified as Prijedor/Banja Luka main road, where those checkpoints were prior to April 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before the 30th of April, the first checkpoint was located at the Omarska intersection. The second checkpoint was at Tunjica near Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Witness P, do we see Tunjica on the map?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you show us, in relation to Omarska, on the map where Tunjica would be, the second checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if we take the distance from Kozarac, you would have to take this road and travel for about 40 kilometres in the direction of Banja Luka, more or less, and then you would come across the Tunjica checkpoint which was set up at the time when the power in Banja Luka was taken over by the red berets, the army. I don't know. Whoever it was. And it was operational until the very last days when I was able to move freely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, but just in the interests of caution, the witness at one point, and I'm not sure of the exact page, indicated where his registration office was. Just for purposes of the transcript, that's at 16.32, I believe. May that be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [No microphone]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Witness P, other than those two checkpoints, prior to April 30th, 1992, were there any other checkpoints on or around the area of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there were joint checkpoints in Gornji Jakupovici, together -- they were also manned by the inhabitants of Babici. There was another joint checkpoint manned by the inhabitants from Kevljani and Omarska. There was another checkpoint near Trnopolje. It was a joint checkpoint manned by the residents from the area. It was at the access road to the village of Babici. There was another checkpoint of that nature in the area of Koncari, although it was not set up on the main road, Prijedor/Banja Luka Road. And at that checkpoint, no controls were made. They were set up on a section of the old Prijedor/Banja Luka Road in a corner, so to speak. And they never ran any checks. I'm referring to the time period until the 30th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for that clarification, as I am as well. Can you tell us the date in which these checkpoints, that you've just identified for us, ceased being manned by the joint entities Serb and Muslim?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that night when Prijedor was taken over, from that night on, the checkpoints were no longer joint checkpoints. They were abandoned by the Serbs, and the next day, there were new checkpoints, 50 or a hundred metres away, which were manned by the Serb residents.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you share with us, sir, the basis for your knowledge that the checkpoints after April 30th were abandoned by the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the 30th of April, a checkpoint appeared in Donja Jakupovici, which was manned solely by Muslims, and Serbs were further away. At one point, I noticed that there were two checkpoints. And on the day before, there was only one checkpoint.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I may be a little confused, and I apologise for that. All I'm asking to know is how you gained the knowledge or information, whether it was direct or from an indirect source, that the Serbs, immediately subsequent to April 30th, 1992, abandoned the checkpoints that we have previously identified as being the joint checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about the checkpoint in Jakupovici on the Prijedor/Banja Luka main road. That morning, I went to Banja Luka very early. I left Kozarac at the time when Kozarac was ostensibly liberated. And while we were having coffee in a company, a woman walked in. She had a lot of cups full of coffee, and she said: "it's my treat. Prijedor has been liberated." When I heard that, I wasn't able to understand what it was all about, and I tried to call my home on the phone. It was impossible because the connections were -- the lines were already down. That day, we were supposed to go to work, but we didn't. We went back home. We passed the Tunjica checkpoint, the checkpoint manned by Serbs near Omarska, and then we went on for another few kilometres. And then we saw the Muslim checkpoint in Jakupovici. We were not stopped either in Omarska or in Jakupovici, at any of these checkpoints. But one could immediately see what was going on. Overnight, there was this extra checkpoint set up.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, when you reference Jakupovici, are you referencing the road as identified as D on the map, D. Jakupovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: The letter "D" refers to lower, Donja Jakupovici, which is near Kevljani and near the railroad. The letter G refers to upper Jakupovici, Gornji Jakupovici, and in my view, this should be the middle part of Jakupovici. But now we're talking about D. Jakupovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Subsequent to April 30th, 1992, when were the checkpoints established which were exclusively Muslim in the area of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few days, or perhaps some of them were set up that very day. The checkpoints simply remained, so to speak, pure because Serbs had left the checkpoints. The checkpoints remained where they were, but there was only one ethnicity manning the checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever, sir, hear from any Serbs that they were kicked out of the checkpoints in the Kozara area after April 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: That night, according to what the people manning the checkpoints said, they all had to go home. They were sick. They said they would come back tomorrow, and they never showed up again.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this, if you may, and you've started to: After April 30th, 1992, can you give us the number of checkpoints that were manned in the Kozara area exclusively by Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if it was more or less than five?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: More than five.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you give me, if the Court permits, an approximation of the number of checkpoints that you believe, as you're sitting here today, there were in the Kozarac area that were exclusively maintained by the Muslims, on or after April 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: The number of checkpoints did not increase after the 30th of April. I think that the Territorial Defence of the Prijedor area has the information about the number of checkpoints. I don't know the exact number, but there were more than five. Whether there were 10, 12, 15, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with respect to Exhibit S51. You've already identified that at the Donja Jakupovici, there was a checkpoint there after April 30th that was manned exclusively by Muslims. Can you tell us where on the main road, if any other checkpoints were established by the Muslims after or manned by the Muslims after April 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you see the blue line here, that's the road linking Gornji Jakupovici through middle Jakupovici, all the way to the railroad. I think that the checkpoint was located about 100 metres away from this area, in the direction of Banja Luka, so it was not on the road itself. It was not a checkpoint, in effect. People were in a field, in a valley so to speak, and they would watch the cars go by on the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Witness P, if you'd be kind enough to just -- and I think I know the road you're referring to -- point on the ELMO, which is to your right, so that we can identify which area you were pointing to as opposed to the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. screen in front of you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: If this is the Kozarac area, then the checkpoint was next to this road here about a hundred metres away from this intersection in the direction of Banja Luka to the north of the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Could you help us identify any other checkpoints within that road and in the area of Kozarac after April 30th, 1992, that existed which were exclusively manned by the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about another one which was manned only by Muslims in Koncari. The next village was a Serb village, Orlovci. These are the only two checkpoints that I saw as I passed through in my car from Banja Luka towards Bosanski Novi.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember, sir, whether or not there was a checkpoint manned exclusively by Muslims in the area depicted on the screen, on this map, S51, as Gutici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so I understand your testimony, sir, because my question may have been awkward, is it your testimony that there was never a checkpoint that was manned exclusively by Muslims after April 30th, 1992, at the area identified as Gutici? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I claim that there was no checkpoint there manned by Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know, sir, if there was a checkpoint at all,, manned exclusively by Muslims after April 30th, 1992, in the area that is west according to this map of Kozarac which is called Kozarusa?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not on the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there one near or about that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a point in the village of Susici. I can't find the road here on this map. And I can't find the village itself. It would be approximately somewhere here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honour, just ask the witness to identify it on the ELMO and not on the screen so I can see where he's pointing to.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the checkpoint was somewhere here, midway between Kozarusa -- on the old road.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you identify us any other checkpoints that you recall, other than those that you've already testified to, which were manned exclusively by Muslims after April 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there were any, I never saw them, and I could not identify their location. For instance, for Trnopolje, for the checkpoint on the way leading to Mrakovica or in Gornji Jakupovici, I never saw these checkpoints and I could not identify the exact location.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Then, sir, help me with this: How do you know that there were at least five such checkpoints on or after April 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I saw three of them, and if I knew that there were some other access routes to Kozarac from Mrakovica, Trnopolje, Gornji Jakupovici, well, there must have been more than five. There were more than five. Or there were five of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Gornji Jakupovici. There was a checkpoint there manned exclusively by Muslims after April 30th, 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And how about the area of Babici? Was there a Muslim checkpoint in the area near or by Babici which was manned exclusively --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure what the situation was like in that place.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And we've already discussed Donja or D. Jakupovici. How about Kamicani? Was there a checkpoint exclusively manned by Muslims after April 30th, 1992 in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about Fotici [sic]? Was there a checkpoint manned by Muslims after April 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw it. And the name is Forici.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I apologize. Forici. I saw it with a'T'. Thank you. Do you know if to the north of Kozarac whether or not there were any checkpoints established after April 30, 1992, that were manned solely and exclusively by Muslims?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there was one. I think. I never went in the direction of Mrakovica in that period, so that's my assumption.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about to the east of Kozarac, the town in the centre of this exhibit S51, do you know if there was a checkpoint on any of the roads that led from the east to Kozarac, other than the ones that you've shared with us already?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you perhaps mention a few places? Place names.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you look on the map, one is like Brdjanin [sic], Tadici, Rajkovici? Any of those?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not sure. I never say them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you ever at any of the checkpoints that were on or around the area of Kozarac after April 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: On one occasion, I was stopped at a checkpoint located near Kozarac. And I stayed there for a few minutes, and then I continued on.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever, sir, assist in the manning of any of the checkpoints on or around the area of Kozarac after April 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did your father?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did any of your two brothers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They didn't. One of my brothers was serving in the Yugoslav People's Army at the time, and my other brother was in the first few days when Kozarac was blocked, in Otika, so he came to Kozarac immediately before the shelling of Kozarac started.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Having passed through some of the checkpoints, as you just described, can you tell us who, and describe the people which manned these checkpoints after April 30th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: The checkpoints were manned by the same people who were manning the checkpoints before. Those were the members of the old Territorial Defence and the local population that lived in the vicinity of the checkpoint. And they had nothing else to do. People would gather there. They would stand around talking to each other, discussing what would happen so that there would always be a group of people standing there at the point.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did the local people that attended or assisted in the manning of the checkpoints subsequent to April 30th, 1992, did they have any uniforms? Did they wear any uniforms? I apologise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: In general, there were no uniforms. The number of weapons that I already spoke about, there would always be a certain number of weapons at the checkpoint. And people with a few rifles would simply stand guard on the checkpoint. That was it, in principal.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I have a few more questions on the checkpoint, and weapons is an area that I hope to cover immediately thereafter. But with respect to who manned the checkpoints, you also stated, I believe, that the same people as before, and then you added as well as the local population. So now with my second question on that, when you say same people as before, isn't it true that the people who manned the checkpoints that you've identified were actually the same people who were manning the checkpoints prior to April 30th, 1992, when the checkpoints were, as I believe you've identified, joint?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a slight difference. Someone from the Territorial Defence of, let's say, Kozarac would perhaps be at the checkpoint in Jakupovici, one or two such persons. And perhaps ten persons from Jakupovici would be with him. That's why I'm saying the Territorial Defence and the local population, for instance, in this case from Jakupovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the people from the Territorial Defence, did they wear any uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had the old military uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were those the same type of uniforms that you saw on the individuals manning the checkpoints prior to April 30th, 1992, or were they in any way different?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: The uniforms remained the same that these people wore, but the people who referred to themselves as the "green berets", some of them had camouflage uniforms that they obtained themselves from somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We'll hopefully discuss the green berets a little later. Is it fair to say, if I'm understanding your testimony correctly, that some of the people who were in the checkpoint after -- strike that. Witness P, is it fair to say that some of the personnel that were manning the checkpoints prior to April 30th, 1992, and were also manning the checkpoints after April 1992, that the uniforms stayed the same? Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So when the checkpoints prior to April 30th, 1992, were manned by the mixed group or both Serbs and Muslims, they wore the identical uniform? A Muslim would have the same uniform as would a Serb; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And is it -- that uniform is what I'd like a description on. Is that the old military uniform you're referring to, or is that actually a uniform which had a blue shirt or blue camouflage on it, if you could help us with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, most of the people were wearing old military uniforms of the SMB olive-drab colour. But sometimes there were some reserve policemen wearing old police uniforms of blue. They may have been present or not. But the blue and the SMB colours were predominant.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was that, sir, true of the personnel which were watching the checkpoints both before April 30th and after April 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: After April 30th, there were more people without uniforms at the checkpoints, and some people with camouflage uniforms calling themselves green berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me broaden my question. Do you know, sir, whether or not there were any other Muslim -- exclusively Muslim checkpoints set up after April 30th, 1992, in the municipality of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, whether or not there was a checkpoint in an area near Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at some checkpoint, an incident took place in Hambarine. Whether it was a joint checkpoint, whether it was a Muslim-manned checkpoint, I cannot tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if I can ask you whether or not you know how long these checkpoints that we were discussing in the Kozarac area, how long they existed after they were set up in early May 1992.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Until -- May 24th until the attack on Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, whether or not -- strike that. Do you know when the checkpoints which were set up after April 30th, 1992, manned exclusively by Muslims in the Kozarac area, do you know when they started to stop vehicles on each of these checkpoints going to Prijedor or going to Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never informed of this, and I knew nothing about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this, if I may, did you, sir, travel from the area of Kozarac to Banja Luka from May 1st, let's say, up until May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, have to pass through any checkpoints from Kozarac through the main road going to Banja Luka from the period of May 1st through May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I had to pass the Jakupovici checkpoint. Well, I was never stopped there at that checkpoint. And I didn't see that anyone else was being stopped. The checkpoint in Omarska, sometimes I would pass it without being stopped. Sometimes I was stopped. The Tunjica checkpoint, I never passed without being stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so I understand, when you were going through Kozarac, through Banja Luka, you were never stopped on any of the checkpoints, and you never saw anyone stopped in the Donja Jakupovici checkpoint. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if I may, can you tell me, if you know, who communicated the ultimatum to the people of the Kozarac area? Was there any individual like the leader of the TO or a politician, if you will, who would have received the ultimatum that you discussed yesterday during your direct that came from the military for safe passage through the main road from Banja Luka to Prijedor? Can you tell us who received that ultimatum?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who was -- who was -- who received this and who ordered that. I think it was ordered via the radio, that all the checkpoints should be removed a few hundreds of metres from the main road, that a convoy would pass, but there was not a convoy in question. It was the attack on Kozarac from two directions, from Prijedor and from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if we may turn to another topic, that's the weapons that we started talking briefly about moments ago, is it fair to state, sir, that the Muslims received the weapons from the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: A part of the weapons were obtained through the Territorial Defence. The old Yugoslav Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there any one individual after April 30th, 1992, which was in charge of the Territorial Defence of Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who was in charge of what Territorial Defence. What I do know is that, for the population census, was Captain Sead, a reservist of the former army, he required lists of people. That is about as far as my knowledge of the command is of the TO of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You testified with respect to the number of automatic guns, I believe, and you described them in some detail yesterday, that the individuals received from the TO, and I believe you said that 400 automatic guns were provided. Is that correct, by the Territorial Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry, could you please quote. I remember it was said 400 rifles probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair. May I proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If you can quote.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll just move to another area. That might help us on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Witness P, if you can help us recollect, can you tell us how many, if any, weapons were issued to the residents of Kozarac by the Territorial Defence on or after April 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have that information. I don't know what was received from the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to assist counsel, I think on page 23 of yesterday's transcript, there were two references to number 400, on line 6 and line 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Page?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On page 23, sir, yesterday, when you were being questioned with respect to the issues of weapons, the question actually starts on the previous page, page 22, where you discuss who were members of the Kozarac Bosnia and Herzegovina army. You started to explain that, and you identify, if I may just read the last sentence there, I think, Your Honour. "So there were groups, and there were 400 rifles all in all at the disposal of the people." And then the question following that: "You mentioned a remark by a policeman about "we can defend ourselves for five minutes." Can you explain a little more about that remark and what value you give to it, whether you agree with it or not?", question. Answer, I believe by you, on line 12, commences by saying: "Well, for someone, 400 rifles was a lot because he was better informed from firing from machine guns on the number of guns, and the number of bultsz" -- I think b-u-l-t-s-z. I know, I have to read it exactly -- "we could make calculation as to the speed, as to how many bullets could be fired from those guns, and we laughed when we heard that. He confronted us with the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. facts." Do you remember giving that testimony about 400 rifles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that I had mentioned 400 rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, can you help me understand whether or not any other weapons were given to the population of Kozarac, namely the Muslim population, respectfully, at that time, by the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about, do you know, whether or not there were a couple of shoulder-launched rocket weapons that were also given by the Territorial Defence to the population, the Muslim population in Kozarac, after April 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never saw any shoulder-launched rocket weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How about, sir, of the approximate 400 automatic guns that may have been given, or do you know anything about them being given to the Kozarac Muslim population by the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, a number of rifles had been bought from the Serb reservists coming back from Croatia, from the battlefield there, and sold rifles to the local population. What the ratio between the received and purchased rifles are, I do not know. I cannot tell you. The only thing I do know, and that I heard about, that there were about 400 rifles. How many automatic, how many semi-automatic, I did not know. And as far as ammunition is concerned, well, some amount was mentioned, but the policemen said: "Well, we can defend ourselves for five minutes, and then we're finished."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may, for the record, just -- and I'm going to quote from your August 26 through 30th, 1994, statement signed September 1st, 1994 specifically page 14, middle of the paragraph of the English text which would be the second formal full paragraph, if I may read that to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to read from a statement that you gave in 1994, and I have copies for whomever needs it. And I will read it in English and they will translate it. Starts in the middle of the page of page 14 as follows: "A lot of the weapons have been spread out by the Territorial Defence army, and a number of the weapons had been bought illegally from the Serbs. A lot of the people had simply taken the weapons with them to the woods where they were hiding. Some of these weapons had been taken to Croatia. According to the statistics, the Territorial Defence army had approximately 400 automatic guns and a couple of shoulder-launched rocket weapons. A person from the army had to register the amount of guns everybody possessed. He was a neighbour of mine and commander of one of the groups, Sead Cirkic. I mentioned him earlier. He had found out there were approximately 400 weapons in the TDF." What I'd like to do, if the usher can just simply have the witness identify whether or not his signature appears on this statement at the bottom of page 14, Your Honour. And just to the record is clear, I'm tendering both the Serbian -- B/C/S, I'm sorry, B/C/S version as well as the English version, but the B/C/S version is not signed, so we're asking him to identify page 14 of the English version. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so we have a clear record, Witness P, you have been handed a document which has the number on the bottom right-hand side 00174138, page 14 in the centre on the bottom, and on the left-hand side, there's a signature there. Is that your signature, sir?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, in light of the time, would this be an appropriate time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. The trial stands adjourned until 5.40.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. And may we proceed immediately with the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness P, although we at the break started to discuss weapons, I have two minor -- or two questions still on the checkpoints. Forgive me for that. My first question in connection with this is, do you know what the purpose of the five or so checkpoints that were in place after April 30th, 1992, that were manned exclusively by Muslims, what was the purpose of those checkpoints?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I never asked myself what the purpose of the checkpoints that existed before the 30th of April was, so I never gave it any deeper thought. The atmosphere of war was prevalent, war was looming, and we were afraid of an attack by Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So help me with this, just as a follow-up, is it that you don't know what the purpose was, or the purpose was to establish a resistance from an attack possibly from the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this was the purpose of the points.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so I'm clear, to establish a resistance in the event of a Serb attack to protect the town of Kozarac or the area of Kozarac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The village of Kozarac, correct, to protect that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the villages around Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: From April 30th, 1992, up until May 23rd, 1992, immediately prior to the attack, as we've defined it, of Kozarac, the day before, were there any attacks by Serbs on any of the Muslim checkpoints in the village of Kozarac and that general territory that we were discussing on Exhibit S51?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And finally, with respect to the checkpoints, I hope I don't have to come back to it, the ultimatum that was actually issued by the military or the convoys, the army convoys, to pass through the main road, was the ultimatum that the checkpoints on the main road move back approximately 100 metres from the main road, or in essence move away from the main road 100 metres?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall the exact distance. The statement was given eight years ago. They had to move back from the main road. Now, as to how far back, I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So would it be fair to say that the military never requested that any of the checkpoints that may have been established in areas such as Gornji Jakupovici, Susici, and Kevljani, they were never asked to be removed because they were not on the main road and thoroughfare from Banja Luka through Kozarac to Prijedor?
