utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether they were too close, I don't know. But it was said that the checkpoints had to be moved further back or to a specified distance, but I don't remember how exactly it went.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Can you tell us if it's correct that the army never requested that the checkpoints established exclusively by the Muslims, on or around the Kozara area, to dismantle from the time of the ultimatum, or to cease to exist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember what happened later and what was being said about other checkpoints.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Actually, my question was with respect to the ultimatum, and I can appreciate that it has been some time, approximately ten years has passed. Do you remember if during the ultimatum there was any suggestion or order by the military to have the Muslim checkpoints dismantle or cease to exist as opposed to asking them to move X number of metres away from the main road as you've testified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they were talking about the passage of the convoy. And as far as I can remember, the checkpoints were to be moved away from the road a few hundred metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Going back to the issue of weapons, if I may, a couple more questions on that, other than the weapons that were received by the general -- or the population in Kozarac, as you've testified, did also some of the Muslim population in the Kozarac area purchase or receive weapons from Serbs?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: A certain number of the overall number of weapons was purchased from Serbs, reservists, and similar persons who engaged in arms trade. And this is how the weapons reached Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what that certain number of overall number of weapons was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know anyone who would?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that either.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the Muslims received or purchased any weapons from Croatians during the time period of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that the weapons were being sold by Serb reservists and similar persons who engaged in arms trade. Serb reservists, sir, can you help me, was it the military reservists or the police reservists or what type of reservists were these Serb reservists that were selling weapons to the Muslims in the Kozara area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: These were military reservists or active-duty servicemen. I never bought any weapons from anyone, but at any rate, weapons were purchased from the troops of the then Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you identify this other group of persons who engaged in arms trade? Who were those people? Were they one and the same, as you've previously identified?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these were Serbs from the villages in the vicinity. They were not in uniforms, so I couldn't say what formation they belonged to, if any. They also brought in weapons in their cars and would offer them up for sale. That's what I meant when I spoke about those other persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And these weapons that were sold by the Serb reservists were sold exclusively to the Muslim residents of Kozarac. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may switch now to a different area, did the Serbs at any time -- strike that. Let's talk about the paramilitary. You mentioned a number of times the "green beret". Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us, Witness P, sir, when the green beret was first established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember the exact date. In the period between the fall of Prijedor, or the liberation of Prijedor, as those who did it, styled it, I would sometimes see a person wearing a uniform with a green beret. They would pass through Kozarac in a car or things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You mentioned on page 21 of yesterday's transcript, approximately line 16 through 22, when asked by the OTP what defence or armed forces were organised in Kozarac --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just wanted to verify the page, Your Honour, from my notes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's correct. Quote the entire paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will. Beginning with the question, Your Honour, if I may?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Line 13, page 21, question: "Can you explain to the Judges what defence or armed forces were organised in Kozarac before the takeover on the 30th of April and after the takeover on the 30th of April?" Answer: "There were people who call themselves green berets, self-styled green berets. There was also a group of Kole's men. They were criminal. There was also a group of Ramiz's men. There was also a man who was expelled from Germany because of drug-related offences. Then there's a note, and it proceeds to say: "They walked around Kozarac armed, wearing green berets. This did not have any kind of political support of the official BH governments or authorities. People simply did it on their own initiative." May I proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I just ask for clarification. You mentioned the name Kole. It's indeed in the transcript. Could the witness please answer the question whether it is stated correctly, the name Kole, or is it another name? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name is Kole. That's a nickname, Kole. And I wouldn't go into the real name of that person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We can go for a moment in private session, because I believe -- I don't know. You mentioned the name before in another statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, my question to you is, the green berets, were they established after April 30th, 1992, or before April 30th, 1992, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, or is it fair to say that they, in fact, did exist after April 1992 -- strike that. Witness P, is it correct that the green berets existed and functioned as a paramilitary group some time after April 30th, 1992, and before May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, how many people or the number of people which were members or participants of these green berets?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if the green berets were limited exclusively to the Kozarac area, or whether or not there were other paramilitary groups known as green berets throughout the Prijedor municipality from April through May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that the green beret is different from the entity that I've identified as the Territorial Defence army? Would that be correct? They are a separate and distinct entity. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether the green berets joined or were included on the list of the population when the Territorial Defence made their list. So my answer to your question is I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know, sir, how many people -- and I apologise if I've asked you this. I seem to have some recollection. How many people were members or participants in the Territorial Defence army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you help us by giving us an approximation, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, so I would rather not mention any figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: (redacted)

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That should be redacted, please. The name, the witness asked for the protection of the name. Therefore, it has to be redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Forgive me, Your Honour, that's fine. If I can just ask the question of the Court on this issue. Since we didn't learn the name, I was just asking the witness who the name of the leader was. And the witness answered in the negative. But that's fine, I don't have a problem with the redaction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Therefore, please be the lines, page 70, line 7 to 9, may the names be redacted there, please. Thank you. Please continue. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you know how many people were members or affiliated with the Kolina's group that we previously discussed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact number.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know an approximation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it true, sir, that the Kolina's group also existed from the period some time after April 30th but before May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will. I apologise. Did this group, Kolina's group, exist as an entity with members in it in the Kozarac area any time during the period of April 30th through May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Similarly, sir, with respect to Ramiz's group, did this group exist, with membership in the Kozarac area, from April 30th through May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the membership or number of members or affiliates the Ramiz's group had during that period of time, April through May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that number either.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know an approximation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, you also mentioned, as we've previously read in the transcript, page 21, line 16, that there was yet another group of a -- I think you said: "Someone who was expelled from Germany because of drug-related offences." Do you recall that testimony? Line 15, page 21.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember mentioning that. I don't remember whether he was a member of these two groups or whether he was operating independently. I can mention his nickname, although it doesn't matter any more because he's not alive anymore. So I don't know if that's of any importance for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It may be. I'd just like to correct my earlier question. It's line 19 in the earlier transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: But I would ask the Court if I'm allowed to ask him the individual's name or identity the group we're referring to now. If I may ask the witness that. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Witness P, help us remember who was the leader, if you will, or who was the entity who you were referring to yesterday, when you identified him as the person who was expelled from Germany because of drug-related offences?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: His nickname was Didin, and I wouldn't really go any further than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. May I ask you, in respect to this individual, Didin, whether that group, Didin's group, if I can call it that, existed from April 30th to May 24th, 1992, in the Kozara area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him in a uniform in that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, how many people were members in the Didin group during that period in the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know an approximation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you describe the uniform that you saw that the individual Didin or any of his members were wearing when you saw him in the Kozarac area during April through May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a grey uniform with a camouflage pattern. It was also bought from the Yugoslav troops that sold not only weapons but uniforms, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: From time to time yesterday, sir, you identified an individual whose name I will not repeat, who was a former captain of the JNA. Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mention his existence in the territory of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And you mentioned his name, I believe. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In fact, at one point, we referenced him, or I believe the OTP did, as a Mr. Cirkin, and you corrected him on the record a couple of times and said it was Mr. Cirkic. Correct? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether his name is actually Cirkin or Cirkic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: For our purposes, may we agree that that's the same individual, we'll refer to him as the former captain in the JNA. Okay? Fair enough?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about that same person, but let's refer to him as Sead for the time being.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. That's fine. Sead, Sead, was he a member of any of the paramilitary or groups that we've just discussed, namely the green berets, Kolina's group, the Territorial Defence army, Ramiz's group, or the Didin group, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if he was a member of any of these groups.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if Sead had his own group which operated and functioned in the territory of Kozarac from April through May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether he was the leader, commander of the whole Territorial Defence of Bosnia and Herzegovina, that was in the making at that time, or somebody else. . . Well, that would be his function at that time, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar, sir, with an entity that's been identified, or commonly referred to as "the Patriotic League" from the Prijedor area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of a squad called the Gariba squad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of the existence of a Trnopolje platoon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of an individual called Suad Garibovic, who was in the Gariba squad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of a squad called the Sivac squad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of an individual called Suto [sic] Sivac, who was purportedly the squad commander of the Sivac squad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you ever hear of a squad by the name of Trnjani, T-R-N-J-A-N-I, squad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you about the groups that I knew. All the groups that you have just mentioned are unknown to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Did you, sir -- one last one, not from a group. I'll pass on the other ones, and thank you for answering the question. Did you know if Becir Medunjanin was a member of the Kozarac Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: He had a function in Kozarac. Now, whether he was a political function in the Crisis Staff, I don't know. I don't know his exact function.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell me if you know when the Crisis Staff in Kozarac was established?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know when it was exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you give us an approximation, if it was before or after May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was probably after the 30th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How did you come to learn the information that some time after April 30th, 1992, there was a Kozarac Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were no stories about this in Kozarac until that moment. This was the date, the 30th. From then on, one began to doubt that -- suspected that something might happen, that an attack was imminent. There were people who were jobless until that day in Prijedor. And we were cut off from Prijedor. We in Kozarac were cut off from Prijedor. And I suppose that in that period of time, a staff had been established or a commission or some body like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So if I gave you the identity of individuals that may have been on the Crisis Staff, can you help me to decide if you knew whether or not they were on the Crisis Staff, or as you sit here, do you have any knowledge of any of the members of the Kozarac Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot tell you with the exception of the name of Becir Medunjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you, if I may return to the former captain of the JNA that we agreed we were going to call him Sead, I have another question with respect to Sead, if I may. Sir, do you know the circumstances of how this former captain of the JNA called Sead left the JNA? Do you know if it was voluntary or involuntary?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At any time, sir, after May 24th, 1992 through October of 1992, did you see Mr. Sead, this former captain of the JNA, at any place where you may have been?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Captain Sead, I saw him at the Manjaca camp when we arrived at the Manjaca camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And sir, isn't it also true that this Captain Sead that we're referring to, the former captain of the JNA, was also with you in the convoy that went to Karlovac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I think that person had been exchanged before we were allowed to go to Karlovac.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, just a couple more questions with respect to these groups that we've identified. Is it true, sir -- well, let me do it by just reading from page 9, the last paragraph of the statement, August 24th through the 30th, 1994, signed September 1st, 1994 by this witness, P. If the Court permits. I don't need the entire paragraph, but I'll read it just for the purposes of its context, because I think those were the rules we've agreed to proceed. Sir, if you can just listen, and it's a little long but I'll try to read it as slow as possible, this paragraph. I have a couple questions in connection with this paragraph. Again, page 9, date stamp number 00174133. "For a month, these groups did exist. They carried the name Kolina's group and Ramiz's group. There was one in the group Kolina. His name was" -- am I permitted to read the name, Judge? I can skip over it. I didn't realise the name was there. There's a name listed. "He was a Muslim, and a captain in the reserve. He was formerly in the Yugoslav army. He tried to join these groups together, and made a list of peoples who were in the groups. Once the area was taken over, these lists were taken into the hands of the Serbians and then to the camps. These groups had started wearing uniforms and walking around Kozarac before the war, but they were not active. They never committed any actions against the Serbs. They never surrendered after the war started. The [sic] hid in the woods. They stayed for four and a half months. Sometimes, they would come down into the villages for food and perhaps they murdered some Serbs then. That is how they continued their existence until they left for Croatia. Before 24 May, before Kozarac was attacked, they never did anything, they never killed anyone or carried out any acts of violence. Before the war, there were Serbs living in the Kozarac area and Serbs in official positions. It would have been very easy for the Serbs to know who these people were and where they lived. They could have arrested them before the war took place if they wanted to, but there were no arrests before the shelling started." End of that paragraph, which proceeds on page 10, two lines on top. With respect, sir, with respect to that, is it fair to say that all of the groups, or you tell me which of the groups that we've identified hid in the woods for four and a half months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can specifically mention Kole, who with about 15 to 20 people, reached Croatia. Which parts of the groups, within those groups, who made up these groups, I don't know. I know that he, with a few others, crossed over to Croatia, to the Croatian side swimming across the Una and then the Sava River. And then they were arrested, all of them, in the area of Glina, or perhaps somewhere else in the area that was under Serb control. And then they were taken to Karlovac or perhaps exchanged. How they got to Karlovac, I do not know. There was a certain number of people who, along with Kole, crossed the Croatian border.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, is it true that you saw this group in Karlovac where you were at subsequent to your release from Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And is it true, sir, that you saw this group that you've just been discussing, Kolina's group, in Karlovac, the same place you were at, after your release from Manjaca?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As you sit here, sir, not having known the specific number or approximate numbers of people in each of these groups, green berets, Kole's group, TO army, Ramiz's group, and Didin's group, do you know how many people actually hid in the woods for four and a half months after May 24, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if any of these individuals in those groups participated at all on an attack that may have happened on the town of Prijedor on, or about, May 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You mentioned in the last sentences of that paragraph, again, if I can just quote that last sentence, bottom of page 9 and then commencing on page 10, the top of your statement of 1994, "they could have arrested them before the war took place if they wanted to, but there were no arrests before the shelling started." Can you tell us who could have arrested whom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kole's group, and the other armed formations, could arrest Serbs in Kozarac, but they never arrested any.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So that statement is in reference to Kolina's group and other groups did not arrest Serbs. Am I understanding you correctly? Or is it that the Serbs, having been in --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Witness P. I didn't finish my question. I just don't want the transcript to be incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think, Your Honour, if I may ask the question for clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think the question is clear enough.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness P. I'll move on. Final question with respect to Sead, this former captain of the JNA, do you know if he's alive currently today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he's alive.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And do you know, sir, whether or not this Sead that we're referencing, if he's back in the Kozarac area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know his exact address.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't want his exact address, but do you know whether he lives currently in the Kozarac area or not?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, his address is perhaps (redacted) I don't know exactly where he lives.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Do you know what his current occupation or title is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think we should go in private session, and redact the words (redacted) page 70, line 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. No objection. [Private session].

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may, Mr. Witness P, I'd like to turn to a different area, although we covered it briefly with respect to the weapons and the paramilitary, and that is the incident that occurred on May or -- approximately on May 22nd, 1992, that you referenced as the Hambarine incident. So I'd like to direct your attention to that if I may. With respect to that, sir, you discussed yesterday that you learned some information in connection with this incident in Hambarine. Can you tell us from whom you learned that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember right now. I think it must have been broadcast on the radio. It was probably announced. There were announcements in regard to Hambarine. I'm not sure, but I think this was done -- that the incident of Hambarine was broadcast on the radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yesterday, on a question that's identified on page 19, lines 24 and 25, with your answer, sir, preceding on page 20, lines 1 through 6, you were asked about this incident, and if I may read the question and answer in its entirety, so that I may refresh your recollection, and I have a couple questions on your answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Witness P, on line 15 -- on page 19, lines 24 and 25 the question is as follows: "On the -- on one day did you become aware of an attack on Hambarine?" Answer, page 20, lines 1 through 6: "Well, before the attack on Kozarac, allegedly there was an incident. It was on the radio that the -- a Serb military vehicle was attacked, that a man was killed, and that everybody had to come in and surrender. What happened in fact, there was an incident. I don't know who really got killed and how many people got killed. But at that time, the shelling of Hambarine began." My question to you, sir, with respect to this answer is you state that there was allegedly an incident in Hambarine, on or about the date that we've identified, in essence, as being May 22nd, 1992. Can you tell me why you think it's only an alleged incident, as opposed to an incident that, in fact, occurred?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if I wasn't present there, an incident remains an incident. And until further information is received, it's always a question about what actually happened. I don't know what is controversial in what I have said. Perhaps I'm not speaking correctly. Perhaps we don't understand each other well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, sir, there's nothing wrong with the way you're speaking or the answers that you've given, so please don't think that. Perhaps I'm just not understanding it, and I'll move on on this issue. Thank you, and I apologise for raising it. What I'd like to know, sir, from your statement that you gave on August 24th through August 30th, 1994, and sign on September 1st, 1992 [sic] -- Forgive me, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I believe it was 1994 you wanted to say. Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. I apologise. Signed on September 1st, 1994. My apologies. Page 6, date stamp 00174130, continuing last paragraph on page 6, continuing on to page 7, date stamp number 00174131, if I may be permitted to quote this paragraph, and then ask the witness whether this is related to or not the Hambarine incident. As follows, as stated on page 6 last paragraph 6 this document: "I may, there were several checkpoints at every village, Serbian and others, and cars were stopped and searched. By May 22nd, a Serbian vehicle came to a Muslim checkpoint without stopping. The guards warned the vehicle to stop, but it didn't, and one of the people in it was killed. The checkpoint was at Hambarine. That started the incidents. On the 23rd May, the Serbs threw a grenade at that checkpoint." We continued to page 7 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, who, if you know, gave you the information with respect to the information that I just read from your statement signed on September 1st, 1994?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whether -- well, I said that I thought it went -- it was broadcast over the radio, although information spread in different ways at the time. Simply, I don't remember exactly who provided that information, and I think it was the information that I provided. And what happened there, I think this was the crux, the very beginning and the reason why the attack on Hambarine started. And I don't think we have to discuss this at length.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. But if you'd permit me just a couple questions on this, just for clarification, is it your testimony, sir, that one grenade, since you used the singular "grenade" in your statement that I've just read were thrown at this checkpoint at Hambarine, or do you have any information with respect to any response from the alleged one person that was killed at that checkpoint on or about May 22nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let us say that the incident in Hambarine was the beginning of the shelling of Hambarine. Can we leave it at that?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll move on from this specific point, but still with respect to Hambarine, if I may, do you know, sir who killed this one person at the checkpoint at Hambarine?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I'm not prepared to admit this question. The witness has already several times stated that it was more or less hearsay from the radio and that he has no other information on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Fair enough, if I may ask just a follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness P, did you hear, subsequent to the incident at Hambarine on May 22nd, 1994, whether there was an investigation as to who started or commenced anything that may have occurred at the so-called incident at the Hambarine checkpoint? Do you know if there was an investigation? I'm sorry, in the record, Mr. Witness P, it says 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. If I can restate the question with your permission. I think it's recorded correctly, I must have misspoke on that. I think I can shorten the question as well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you know of any investigation relating to the Hambarine incident after May 22nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may, sir, switch, two days later, we're talking now about the ultimatum for you that was given by the military for an army convoy to pass through Kozarac, do you know whether or not that army convoy was going to Prijedor or to Hambarine, two days after the incident on Hambarine, namely May 22nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: That convoy never should have passed through Prijedor. Those were two armed columns that attacked Hambarine. One from Prijedor, and the other from Banja Luka. The existence of this column was a pretext for ordering the removal of the checkpoints from the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me, if you may, why do you believe that that convoy "never should have passed through Prijedor"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, its passage was never noticed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to this army convoy and the ultimatum that occurred on May 24th, 1992, do you know, sir, or have any information whether or not any of the military personnel who were on the convoy, specifically the very first truck that was leading the convoy, whether or not any Serb military men were killed on or about May 24th, 1992 while passing through the checkpoints in Donja Jakupovici, or anywhere through the Kozarac territory?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I would object to the question, because the witness has indicated the convoy didn't pass through the checkpoints. He indicated these convoys attacked Kozarac. So the implication that the convoys simply passed through the checkpoints in the question is not in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sustained.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may try to restate the question, Your Honour, to avoid the technical objection offered by my learned friend from the Office of the Prosecutor. I'll try my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did the convoy, sir, get through and pass the area known as Donja Jakupovici?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the convoy, when approaching Jakupovici, began firing at the people who had been a few hundreds of metres away, a few -- where the checkpoint had been removed a few hundred metres away from the road. Later on, during our stay in the Omarska camp, it was stated that someone from that checkpoint hit someone from the army who was in the first vehicle of that column, that first started firing against the people and the neighbouring houses. That is as much as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. My question to you, sir, on this main road that we've identified on Exhibit S51, and I understand you don't have it in front of you, the main road, the Prijedor/Banja Luka main road, did this convoy continue to proceed towards, not through and to Prijedor, towards Kozarac and actually get to the area known as Kozarusa, if you know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that convoy continued to act in a military fashion slightly in the direction of Kozarac, and from the Prijedor side near the Kozarusa area, they went very slightly. They were firing. The tanks were also in the convoys, that also fired. It was not one convoy, two convoys from two sides, an organised attack against Kozarac. This is how I see how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If the Court would please ask the usher to have S51 brought back to the ELMO. I'm sorry, Your Honour. May I proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Witness P, now having S51 in front of you, a question I hope is simple and straightforward. I'm not asking anything more than this: Did the convoy that was coming from Banja Luka, through the main road of Prijedor/Banja Luka main road, which stopped you said approximately and, correct me if I am wrong, at the D. Jakupovici area, that general area, did that convoy coming in that direction, did it ultimately turn back or continue forward on the road of Prijedor/Banja Luka main road towards Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that it continued. It continued along the road to Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So in fact, it continued all the way up to what's in the centre of Exhibit S51 identified with a blue dot with the name on it "Kozarac." Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how -- I wouldn't know how long this movement lasted and what the duration was. But the official fall of Kozarac was on the 26th, and the column either went left or right from the main road. Everything was occupied. Everything was blocked. It was a convoy that intended to take over Kozarac and not to pass through Kozarac, and this is how -- and this is what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know how it came about that there was a surrender of the town of Kozarac on or about May 26th, 1992 -- village, I'm sorry. The village of Kozarac.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: The whole region of Kozarac was under siege, encircled from the takeover of power in Prijedor. So this was a small ghetto from which one could reach Prijedor, despite the various checkpoints, and the encirclement of Kozarac started when the -- with the seizure of power in Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So it's your testimony, if I understand you correctly, that the seizure of Kozarac started approximately three weeks prior to the attack, on or about April 30th, 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The blocking of the access routes to Prijedor, preventing the Muslim people going to work to Prijedor, automatically meant that Kozarac was under siege.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Other than that one individual who was in the front of the convoy that was killed coming through the main road of Prijedor/Banja Luka, do you know of any other instances where a Serb military person was shot or killed, who was in that convoy coming from Banja Luka through the Prijedor/Banja Luka main road, on or about May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard, later in the camp, people say that around Forici, there was some shooting, that fire was opened on military vehicles. As to the accuracy of these stories, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I appreciate that, sir. But in this Forici area, did you learn from any person while you were detained whether or not any other individuals were shot or killed who were on this convoy coming from Banja Luka on the Prijedor/Banja Luka main road on May 24th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I spoke about that. I'm not sure any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So is it fair to say that, as you sit here today, you don't know other than this one individual who was at the front of the convoy as being, according to what you learned, the only individual that was shot and killed in this convoy. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember what I stated in 1994. It has been eight years. Whether several people were killed or just this one person, I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Witness P, all I want to know is what you remember today. And if you don't remember any more, that's fine. Thank you. I asked you earlier, and respectfully, I don't know if I understood the answer. My mistake, on the question. My question earlier was, was there an agreement, or if you could describe for us: How was it the surrender of Kozarac came about on or about May 26th, 1992? A couple questions ago, sir, I apologise if you answered it. I did not understand the answer if you could help me with that. Was it a negotiated settlement, or did everyone just throw up their arms, or if you could just describe for me how it came about?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether this is 100 per cent correct, but I am convinced that the information was relayed through the Kozarac Police Station, and they probably obtained it through the police radio network, and they were in contact -- they were able to establish contact with Prijedor. And that was the way that the information came in that the surrender would take place and that the police weapons would be taken to Prijedor and that people would also head to Prijedor. I'm not sure, but at one point, there was so much information coming in, and people were moving about so much that one could not tell what was true, what was not true. But I think that this came in through the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And in fact, as a result of that information that you received from the police, the people, including yourself and your wife, among others, you proceeded to go where the authorities in Kozarac told you to go, and then joined this second, if I can call it that, convoy heading to Prijedor. Correct? On or about May 26th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the time when first information was received from the police, I partly believed it, partly I didn't believe it. When I got home, I spent some time there, at home. I don't know exactly how much time, but at that time, the military jeep had already come to the yard, and they gave us the same information, that we all had to head towards Prijedor with all the people that were in my house at that time. We didn't ask them what direction we should take, what route to take. We simply took off. And that's how we reached the Kozarac intersection, where we encountered the tank and a lot of troops and the police officers and things became quite clear to us then.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Back to the military jeep, were there more than one person in that jeep who was giving you these instructions?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that there was one of the people that they had found in the same way that they found us, and they -- he had to take them to a house where they supposed the civilians were, in houses or in garages.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What was the ethnicity of this individual in the military jeep?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civilian was a person from Kozarac. He was a Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: At any time during the gathering of the individuals and the people from the Kozara area which were going to proceed, as indicated, to Prijedor, at any time did you confront or see any Serb military personnel on May 26th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from the jeep and the persons there, until the -- until we came to the intersection in Kozarac, I didn't see any armed people. When we reached the Kozarac intersection, I saw armed people there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just for clarification, when you say "armed people," are you referring to armed Serbs and Muslims, or armed Serbs, or just tell me what you're referring to so the record is clear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Armed Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In this convoy that proceeded through Kozarac that you were a part of that took the route a little south and then it came up north, as you described for us yesterday, from Kozarac, did this convoy contain any of the Bosnian Muslim men who were participants or affiliated with any of the four or five paramilitary groups we've previously identified; namely, the green beret, Kolina's group, Ramiz's group, Didin's group, and the patriotic league, and the Territorial Defence army?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everybody was a member of the territorial army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, at least on paper. So one could even say that I was a member of the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's fair, sir. I apologise. I wanted to actually exclude that, and I didn't. Other than the Territorial Defence army, those other five groups that we've identified, the green beret, Kolina's, Ramiz's group, patriotic league, and Didin's group, were any members of those groups part of the convoy that proceeded from Kozarac with you and your Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. family and your wife towards Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS P [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I note the time. I have actually two other areas to cover and I would be willing to share with the Court. One is the witness's detention in Trnopolje, and also Omarska, and just briefly, a little on Manjaca, but I don't know. I can ask a couple more questions if the Court wants me to. They are just new areas. Whatever the Court's pleasure is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I believe there are numerous questions open and, therefore, we should have a break. But we shouldn't call it a day before we have resolved two more or less technical questions. The first one is yesterday, you said you would comment on Document 52B. Any objections on the admission into evidence, the document that was read out?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: 52, no, Judge, we do not have an objection since the witness identified the individual, and that was our concern for purposes of foundation. So no, we do not have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Then 52B, admitted into evidence. And it is agreed that we don't need any additional translation because we have it in the transcripts. I see nodding from both sides. Then no interpretation needed. And finally, the Office of the Prosecutor took the Document 2F from the series of photographs and evidently tendered this document. And therefore, this should go as S15-23. And I don't see any objections from the Defence to this. Therefore, it's admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: One other minor matter to inform the Trial Chamber, the Trial Chamber had asked the witness Dr. Cehajic to have a document delivered to the Tribunal through the Office of the Prosecutor. And apparently, that has arrived although it's partly illegible. I don't know if it came by fax. But the information I have is that the copy is partly illegible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We'll come back to this. Do you want to comment in open session why there is an exchange of witnesses, of upcoming witnesses, especially as regards Witness 8, if I remember correctly?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes, I can say it in open session. Actually, I prefer to do it in -- we've made a decision not to call Witness 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So we can strike Witness 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Any other observations?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Not with respect to this, but we do have one from an earlier mentioned observation in connection with the Document Exhibit S52. I'm not sure if we're going to get the other documents that the witness had or not. I'm just truly unclear as to what the Court's position was on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Put it this way: We have a meeting tomorrow, 11.30. And then the trial stands adjourned until tomorrow, 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: 7.00 p.m., to be reconvened on Friday, the 24th day of May, 2002, at 2.15 p.m.
